This guide takes you from an assessment project folder to a tested ZIP for
PSYC40940. Read it alongside the [summative assessment brief](https://now.ntu.ac.uk/d2l/le/lessons/1174881/topics/15225379) and grading matrix
in the current NOW learning room. Use the current brief and Dropbox to check
the deadline and any year-specific instructions.

## What you are preparing

The final portfolio combines one RMarkdown report and a separate Shiny app,
using one suitably rich behavioural dataset.

| Component | What it needs to do |
|---|---|
| RMarkdown report | Generate four different static visualisation types, with clear presentation and commentary explaining the design choices |
| Reflection in the same report | Discuss decisions, challenges, trade-offs and practical constraints in your own words |
| Separate Shiny app | Provide at least two useful interactive plots and meaningful user inputs, with at most three tabs |
| Reproducible project | Supply source, rendered report, data or an approved access route, and required supporting files |
| AI declaration | Include the completed [form supplied on NOW](https://now.ntu.ac.uk/d2l/le/lessons/1174881/topics/15126556) |

Shiny plots that update when users change filters or selections meet the
interactivity requirement. Plotly is an option, rather than a compulsory
package. The report and app should each explain what their views help readers
learn about the behavioural data.

The current word limit is 2,000 across report text, figure commentary/captions,
dashboard explanatory text and reflection. Code, references/bibliography, raw R
output and data-file contents are excluded. Check the current brief before
submission.

## 1. Create or open your assessment project

Keep the assessment in a self-contained project folder. If your formative
assessment already has a suitable project, you may develop that project for the
summative. Keep only the final report and app versions in the submission copy.

To start a dedicated project in RStudio:

1. Choose File > New Project > New Directory > New Project.
2. Enter a neutral directory name such as `behavioural-portfolio`.
3. Choose a location you can find again and click Create Project.
4. Check that `behavioural-portfolio.Rproj` appears in the Files pane.
5. Open this `.Rproj` file whenever you return to the assessment.

If your assessment files already occupy a dedicated folder without a project
file, use File > New Project > Existing Directory and select it. A class-work
project containing all weekly materials needs a clean assessment copy before
submission.

The `.Rproj` file stores project settings. The Rmd, app, data and supporting
files remain separate files inside the project folder. In Tools > Project
Options > General, disable restoring a saved workspace and choose not to save
the workspace on exit. Code must load and prepare the data it needs.

## 2. Put data and supporting files inside the project

1. Use New Folder in the Files pane to create `data`.
2. Copy the actual data files used by the report and app into it.
3. Record the source and document what one row and the relevant variables mean.
4. Use relative paths that match the supplied folder and filenames exactly.

For a CSV called `behaviour.csv`, a report saved in the main project folder
could contain:

```{r csv-import-example, eval=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
my_data <- read_csv("data/behaviour.csv")
```

Use your actual filename. Match the import function to its format: an Excel
`.xlsx` needs a function such as `readxl::read_excel()`. Changing a filename's
extension does not convert its contents. Keep preparation steps explicit in
code, including filtering, recoding and calculations used by the figures.

Paths to your own Downloads or Desktop will not locate files on the marker's
computer. Match folder-name case, including `data` versus `Data`. Include
bibliography, citation-style, image and helper files if your report or app uses
them.

If data are too large to submit or cannot legally be redistributed, the brief
permits a stable URL or DOI, clear access/download instructions, and import or
preparation code where possible. Explain this in the report and include a short
data-access README with the exact files and their expected locations. State any
registration requirement and check access arrangements with the module leader
in advance if needed.

## 3. Create the report Rmd

1. Choose File > New File > R Markdown and select HTML output.
2. Use a meaningful title about the data or question and leave the author field
   empty for anonymous submission.
3. Save the file as `report.Rmd` in the main project folder, beside `.Rproj`.
4. Replace the demonstration content with your own report, keeping one YAML
   header at the top.

You may develop your formative Rmd instead of starting again. Your submission
must contain exactly one final report Rmd. Replace remaining template
instructions, example questions and unrelated dataset descriptions.

Use Markdown text for your narrative and reflection. Use the Insert menu above
the Rmd editor to add R chunks for package loading, data import, preparation and
figures. Use unique chunk names. Bring the final static-figure code into this
report; the rendered figures should be generated when it is knitted.

Include the dataset source and observation unit, the questions the plots
address, interpretations, reasons for design choices and what those choices
conceal. Give figures meaningful labels, units and captions and cite relevant
sources. Put the static visualisations and reflection in this same document.

At the end of the report, include an R chunk containing:

```{r package-version-example, eval=FALSE}
sessionInfo()
```

This records R and package versions. Keep its output in the rendered report;
an equivalent package/version summary is also acceptable under the brief.

## 4. Save the Shiny app separately

Save your final dashboard as `app.R`. A simple arrangement puts it in the main
project folder, beside `report.Rmd` and the `.Rproj` file. If you are developing
one of the weekly app scripts, save your final adapted version under this name.
Finish any `---` completion blanks before testing.

The app needs its package-loading and data-import code as well as its UI,
server and `shinyApp(ui, server)` call. It must not depend on data objects
created by running the report first. For the simple folder arrangement shown
below, both report and app can read `data/behaviour.csv`.

Test the components using their own controls in RStudio:

| Component | How to test it |
|---|---|
| `report.Rmd` | Save it and choose Knit to create the report |
| `app.R` | Open the whole script and choose Run App |

After editing the app, save it, stop the running app and use Run App again.
Keep it running while testing its controls. The report should knit separately
without launching the Shiny app.

An existing working app folder is also accepted. Keep its structure, with
`app/app.R` and its support files, and check the data paths from that folder.
For example, `app/app.R` uses `../data/behaviour.csv` to reach a sibling `data/`
folder, whereas a root-level `app.R` uses `data/behaviour.csv`. Choose one final
app arrangement and test it as supplied.

## 5. Render and inspect the report

1. Save `report.Rmd` and click Knit.
2. Check that `report.html` appears in the project folder.
3. Open it and inspect all four static visualisation types, captions, labels,
   references, reflection and package/version information.
4. Fix the source where necessary, then knit again after your final edits.

HTML is the expected report format. PDF is acceptable for a good reason under
the brief; its Rmd source is still required. Submit the final output generated
by the final Rmd.

The report and app should each list and load their required packages. Install
packages once before testing; package installation should not run every time
the report is knitted or the app starts. Keep any required `report_files/` or
other resource folders generated alongside the HTML.

## 6. Complete the AI declaration from NOW

1. Open the [GenAI/AI usage declaration form on NOW](https://now.ntu.ac.uk/d2l/le/lessons/1174881/topics/15126556).
2. Download the form provided there.
3. Complete it. In its explanation of AI use, describe how you used any tools
   for permitted support such as code development or debugging. If you did not
   use GenAI, state that.
4. Save the completed form in the assessment folder in the format requested
   on NOW. The example below uses `ai-declaration.pdf`.
5. Include it in the final ZIP.

Use the official form and follow its specific instructions, including any
required identification fields. Your submitted commentary, interpretation,
reflection, design rationale and explanations must be your own work. GenAI is
not a reference source, and you need to understand and justify assisted code.

## 7. Make a clean submission copy

Keep your working project as a backup. Make a submission copy in a separate
location, containing the final files only. For a root-level app, it could look
like this:

```text
behavioural-portfolio/
  behavioural-portfolio.Rproj
  report.Rmd
  report.html
  app.R
  ai-declaration.pdf
  data/
    behaviour.csv
  references.bib       (if used)
  apa.csl              (if used)
```

| Required item | Check in the submission copy |
|---|---|
| One final report Rmd | Contains static-figure code, commentary and reflection |
| Its rendered HTML | Shows the final figures and text; PDF is an allowed exception |
| `.Rproj` file | Opens this assessment project |
| Separate final Shiny app | Either root-level `app.R` or the complete app folder |
| Relevant data | Match the import paths; include the documented access alternative if applicable |
| Required support files | Bibliography, style, images, helpers and HTML resource folders where used |
| Completed AI declaration | The form downloaded from NOW, completed and saved |

Remove class slides, exercise/session guides, unused app versions, extra Rmds,
old report outputs and unrelated data from this copy. Exclude `.RData`,
`.Rhistory` and the temporary `.Rproj.user/` directory. Keep helper scripts
that your report or app actually calls.

Check anonymity throughout the report, app, filenames, project name and
submitted documentation. Keep your name and N number out unless specifically
instructed otherwise; follow the declaration form's own requirements. Use
relative paths so your code does not print or depend on personal file paths.

## 8. Create the ZIP

Save everything and close the project. In your computer's file manager,
compress the whole submission copy of the `behavioural-portfolio` folder.

| Computer | How to create the archive |
|---|---|
| Windows | Right-click the folder and choose ZIP compression. If needed, use Show more options > Send to > Compressed (zipped) folder. |
| Mac | Control-click or right-click the folder and choose Compress. |

The result is a file such as `behavioural-portfolio.zip`. Keep the directory
structure inside it so the code can find its inputs.

## 9. Test the extracted ZIP

1. Extract the ZIP into a new location. On Windows, use Extract All; on Mac,
   double-click the ZIP and use the extracted folder.
2. Open the `.Rproj` in the extracted copy, outside the ZIP itself.
3. Choose Session > Restart R.
4. Knit the extracted `report.Rmd`, then inspect the new rendered output.
5. Restart R again. Open the extracted `app.R` and use Run App without first
   running the report. If using an app folder, open that folder's `app.R`.
6. Test each input and every tab, the plots and counts, and any empty-selection
   feedback. Restore a valid selection and check that outputs recover.
7. Check that the completed AI declaration and all support files are present.

This tests the files the marker will receive. If you find a problem, repair
your working project, rebuild the submission copy and ZIP, and retest the new
ZIP. Fixing only the extracted test copy will not repair the ZIP you upload.

## 10. Check the brief and upload

Before submission, confirm that:

- the report includes four different useful static plot types and your design
  commentary;
- the same report includes your reflection and a package/version summary;
- the separate app supports meaningful exploration with at least two
  interactive plots, user inputs and at most three tabs;
- both components work from the extracted project and explain the behavioural
  data clearly;
- the source, rendered report, project, app, inputs/support files and completed
  AI declaration are inside one ZIP;
- the word limit and anonymity instructions have been checked against the
  current brief.

Upload the tested ZIP to the summative Dropbox in NOW by the current deadline.
Finish the submission process, check its confirmation and keep the receipt/email
and exact ZIP. Plan time for this final test and upload rather than leaving
packaging until the deadline.
